summary: Campbell packs roughly 43,000 people into just six square miles on the flat Santa Clara Valley floor, yet it managed to hold onto a compact, walkable downtown centered on Campbell Avenue — a stretch of independent coffee shops, restaurants, and a weekly farmer's market — that most Silicon Valley cities its size long ago surrendered to strip-mall sprawl. The geography is almost entirely level, with the Santa Cruz Mountains visible to the west and the Diablo Range to the east, giving clear-sky evenings a wide gradient of color without requiring a hillside address. At a median home price of $1,550,000 against a median household income of around $147,000, the price-to-income ratio exceeds 10:1, meaning even substantial earners face steep math on a purchase; median rent near $2,750 absorbs a smaller but still serious share. The local economy leans heavily on the broader Silicon Valley tech and healthcare ecosystem — eBay and Pruneyard Shopping Center sit within or adjacent to city limits — so job-switching without relocating is plausible, and commutes along Highway 17 or the Los Gatos Creek Trail (which threads north–south through town for biking) keep options flexible. With 9.6 hours of daily sunshine on average and highs hovering around 71°F year-round, outdoor routines rarely get disrupted. Campbell functions as a small-town grid stitched into a mega-region's economy — convenient and distinctly itself, but priced as though the entire valley is bidding on every block.
